extracted.intended_audience: applicants and agents preparing/filing PCT Chapter II (international preliminary examination) demands
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and filing a demand for international preliminary examination (Chapter II PCT), including eligibility, timing, form/content, translations, amendments, representation and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to international preliminary report (Chapter II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerning access to the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II of the PCT), the International Bureau, if so requested by an elected Office, makes copies of that report available on PATENTSCOPE to third parties on behalf of that Office, but not before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A number of elected Offices have made this request to the International Bureau; the International Bureau also makes related documents received from the IPEA under PCT Rule 71.1(b) available on PATENTSCOPE (see paragraph 10.079A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of copies of international application to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau communicates a copy of the international application in the language in which the international application is published, to each designated Office upon their request and at the time specified by that Office, pursuant to Rule 93bis, but not prior to the international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publication language differs from the filing language, the IB will furnish, upon request, a copy in the filing language. The IB sends Form PCT/IB/308 notices at 19 and 28 months to inform the applicant which Offices were sent the communication; those notices are conclusive evidence that communication took place on the specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early transmittal of copy to designated Offices before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the international application may be communicated by the International Bureau to any designated Office prior to international publication, but not before the expiration of one year from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such special transmittal requires payment of a fee (Annex B (IB)). Transmittal in this way does not, unless expressly requested, entitle the designated Office to start processing. If the applicant requests early commencement of national processing, IB will effect the communication upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and evaluation criteria of international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination provides 'a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on the questions whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (to be non‑obvious), and to be industrially applicable' (Article 33(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is carried out by an IPEA at the request (demand) of the applicant for use before elected Offices. Not every international applicant has the right to file a demand; eligibility rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of requesting international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand for international preliminary examination gives the applicant the opportunity to evaluate chances of obtaining patents in elected Offices and normally delays the national phase in each elected State until the expiration of 30 months from the priority date (provided the demand is submitted before 19 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer times may apply in some elected Offices; see national Chapters and paragraph 10.010 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and third‑party access to IPEA file
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for the fact that a demand has been filed and names of States with notices of withdrawal, the international preliminary examination procedure remains confidential between the applicant, the IPEA and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after 1 July 1998, copies of documents in the IPEA file (except information omitted from publication following a reasoned request) may be obtained by third parties via elected Offices whose national law provides file access. See paragraphs 9.016A, 10.080–10.081 and 11.072–11.074.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to submit a demand (residence/nationality and filing Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two conditions for a demand: (1) the applicant (or at least one of multiple applicants) must be a resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II; and (2) the international application must have been filed with the receiving Office of, or acting for, a Contracting State bound by Chapter II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, at the time the demand is made, no applicant is a resident or national of a State bound by Chapter II (e.g., due to change in applicants), the right to make a demand is lost and the demand is considered not to have been submitted. Concepts of residence and nationality defined in Rule 18.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which States are elected by filing a demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of the demand constitutes the election of all Contracting States which are designated and are bound by Chapter II of the Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States whose designation has been withdrawn cannot be elected; an election may be withdrawn after filing. Withdrawal of a designation that has been elected entails withdrawal of the corresponding election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit the demand (competent IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must be submitted separately from the international application and directly to an IPEA which is competent to carry out international preliminary examination on the international application concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each receiving Office specifies one or more competent IPEAs. Competence may depend on the receiving Office, the language of filing and which ISA carried out the search. If several IPEAs are competent, the applicant may choose among them. Consult Annexes C and E for competent Authorities and accepted languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of demands filed with non‑competent Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a demand is submitted to a receiving Office, an ISA, an IPEA which is not competent, or the International Bureau, that Office/Authority or the IB will mark it with the date of receipt, which will be considered the date of receipt on behalf of the competent IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The non‑competent Office or the IB may forward the demand to the competent IPEA or to the IB for forwarding (Rules 59.3(a),(b),(c),(e),(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of competent IPEA when multiple Authorities are competent
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more IPEAs are competent, the Office or Authority receiving the demand (or the IB) will invite the applicant to indicate the competent IPEA within the applicable time limit; if the applicant indicates, the demand will be transmitted promptly; if not, the demand is considered not to have been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indication must be made within the Rule 54bis.1(a) time limit or within 15 days from invitation, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for submitting a demand
rubrics_metrics.description: A demand may be submitted at any time prior to the expiration of the later of: (i) three months from transmittal to the applicant of the international search report and written opinion (or declaration no ISR will be established); or (ii) 22 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To secure full effect in some Offices the demand must be submitted before 19 months. The international preliminary report must, in most cases, be established before 28 months from priority date, or six months from the start time of examination, or six months from receipt by the IPEA of any translation—whichever expires last. Filing the demand as soon as possible after evaluating the ISR and written opinion gives more time and better quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for IPEA when filing/publishing language not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where neither the language in which the international application was filed nor the language in which it is published is accepted by the IPEA, the applicant must furnish with the demand a translation of the international application into a language both accepted by that Authority and a language of publication (Rule 55.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No translation required where the ISA and IPEA are part of the same national Office or intergovernmental organization; the translation used for the international search may be relied upon. See Annex E for languages accepted by each IPEA and paragraph 9.010 for translations of Article 19 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, contents and language of the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must be made on a printed form to be filled in or presented as a computer print‑out complying with the Administrative Instructions; downloadable PDF (PCT/IPEA/401) is available. The demand may also be filed online via ePCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The demand is available in multiple languages. Sample filled‑in forms and copies may be obtained free from the receiving Office or the IPEA. The demand must identify the applicant and the international application, contain a petition for IPE, statements concerning amendments and indication of language, and must be signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must be in the language of the international application or, if the application was filed in a different language than publication, in the language of publication; if a translation is required for the IPEA, the demand must be in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where more than one IPEA is competent, identify the chosen Authority (name or two‑letter code) on the first sheet of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification details required on the demand (Box I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must be identified by its international application number, filing date and title (Rule 53.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the international application number is not yet known, indicate the receiving Office with which it was filed. The title must be the same as in the published international application (same as in the request unless modified by the ISA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional file reference and priority date recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to indicate a file reference (if any) not exceeding 25 characters; indication of the priority date on the demand is not mandatory but recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the priority date assists the IPEA to ascertain promptly whether the demand was filed before the 19‑month time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identification and residency information (Box II)
rubrics_metrics.description: If sole applicant, that applicant must be a resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II; if there are multiple applicants, at least one must be such a resident or national. Detailed indications (full names, addresses, contact details, nationality and residence) follow Rule 4 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a question of residence or nationality arises, the IPEA will request the receiving Office or national Office to decide and will inform the applicant; the applicant may submit arguments directly to that Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording changes in applicant name/person prior to filing demand
rubrics_metrics.description: If a change in name or person has been requested to be recorded under Rule 92bis.1 before the demand was filed, the applicant(s) on record at the time the demand is filed must be indicated in the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 11.018–11.022 for Rule 92bis.1 details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification by e‑mail (Box II and III)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an e‑mail address is indicated in Box II (applicant) or Box III (agent), the International Bureau and the IPEA (if providing the service) will send notifications by e‑mail; where an agent has indicated an e‑mail address, notifications will only be sent to the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all Authorities will send e‑mail notifications. If no e‑mail is provided or applicant chooses postal mail, notifications will be sent by post. Applicant/agent must keep e‑mail details up‑to‑date and ensure incoming e‑mails are not blocked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and agents (Box III)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is not obliged to be represented before the IPEA but may be represented by an agent (recommended). The agent may be the one used for filing or another who has the right to practice before the receiving Office; an agent may also be appointed specifically for IPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An already appointed agent may sign the demand; a different agent or additional agent may be designated in the demand or by separate power of attorney. If an agent is registered with the IPEA, the registration number may be indicated. Power of attorney filing requirements may be waived by the receiving Office, IB or IPEA in some cases. See paragraphs 11.001–11.014 for more on representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to common representatives at earlier stages continue to apply during IPE; if no common agent or representative appointed, the first‑named applicant may be deemed common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate power of attorney must be filed with the IPEA, IB or receiving Office if the person appointed signs the demand on behalf of the applicant, unless the requirement is waived. See Annexes B (IB), C and E for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend before and during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has the right under Article 34(2)(b) to amend the claims, the description and the drawings before the start of IPE and also during the examination, if time permits, until preparation of the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the second opportunity to amend claims (first was Article 19). See paragraphs 10.028, 10.067–10.071 and 11.045–11.047 for details on amendments under Article 34(2)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing statement concerning amendments and language (Box IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement concerning amendments should be completed to enable the IPEA to identify documents which will serve as the basis for starting IPE; completing the indication of language helps determine whether the demand and application are in a language accepted by the IPEA or whether a translation is required (Rule 53.2(a)(iv), Rule 53.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete the statement is not fatal: if no amendments are filed and none intended, IPE will start on the basis of the application as originally filed. However, failure to indicate existing amendments or to indicate an intention to file amendments may delay start or prevent amendments being taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to complete the statement concerning amendments (specific check‑boxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendments to the claims were made under Article 19 prior to filing the demand, the statement must indicate whether those amendments should be taken into account or considered reversed by an Article 34 amendment. If no Article 19 amendments have been made but the time to file them has not expired, the statement may indicate that the applicant wishes the start of IPE to be postponed. If Article 34 amendments are submitted with the demand, the statement must so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed explanation is given for each check‑box in Box IV; marking the appropriate box affects whether and when the IPEA starts examination and whether particular amendments will be considered as the basis for examination.
